title: Basic Math Operations
body:
Doing Math with Code

Computers were originally invented to do lightning-fast mathematics. In Python, you can perform addition (+) and subtraction (-) using numbers and Variables (Lesson 2.1) ↗.

Two Mental Models for Addition

Analogy A — Two Boxes Added: x + y takes the number out of box x, takes the number out of box y, adds them, and stores the total in a new result box.

Analogy B — A Cash Register: Each variable represents an item's price. Adding variables is like the cash register totaling up your shopping cart.

Example: Addition & Subtraction
# Addition
price1 = 50
price2 = 20
total = price1 + price2
print(total)  # Displays 70

# Subtraction (Discount)
discount = 15
final_price = total - discount
print(final_price)  # Displays 55

Brackets and Evaluation Order

When you write complex math, Python evaluates expressions from left to right for operators of equal priority. You can use brackets () to group parts together and tell Python which calculation to do first:

Example: Using Brackets
result = (10 + 5) - 3
print(result)  # (15) - 3 = 12

Important: Numbers vs Quotes

Remember from Integers vs Strings (Lesson 2.2) ↗: Numbers for math must NOT have quotes. Writing "10" + "5" will glue the text together as "105" instead of doing math!
